themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 46 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 14.9 per week (209% increase, z-score: 6.27), suggesting a widespread pavement or infrastructure failure across Bed-Stuy requiring urgent investigation into whether recent weather or construction triggered the spike.
evidence: Street condition complaints: 46 this week vs. 14.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.27, 209% increase)
Concurrent spike in lot condition complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.2 avg (1500% increase)
Concurrent spike in street sign missing: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 avg (2300% increase)
reporting_angles: Boots on ground: photograph and map damaged streets and signs across Bed-Stuy; interview residents about specific problem blocks
NYC DOT accountability: did recent weather events (snow/ice from prior week) go unrepaired, or is this a maintenance backlog issue?

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints hit 6 THIS WEEK against a baseline of 1.0 per week (500% increase, z-score: 7.07), indicating either coordinated unauthorized tree removal or a discrete incident requiring investigation into who is damaging street trees and why.
evidence: Illegal tree damage complaints: 6 this week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.07, 500% increase)
No recent local news coverage; suggests story is underreported
5 active ULURP applications in district pipeline (rezoning and development projects) could trigger tree removal activity
reporting_angles: Investigate whether construction/development projects (1166 Bedford Ave, 862-868 Kent Ave rezoning, Park Avenue Brooklyn rezoning) are clearing trees without permits
Interview NYC Parks and NYC Department of Environmental Protection on enforcement: how many violations issued, who filed the 311 complaints?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes piling up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week (860% increase, z-score: 7.72), signaling either a bike-share docking crisis, a disposal/storage problem, or organized dumping that warrants street-level verification.
evidence: Abandoned bike complaints: 6 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72, 860% increase)
No Reddit discussion or local news coverage yet
Potential correlation with concurrent spike in dirty condition complaints (117 two weeks ago vs. 35.9 avg)
reporting_angles: Walk streets and document abandoned bikes: are they Citi Bikes, personal bikes, or broken bikes left for disposal?
Contact Citi Bike (Motivate) for explanation: is there a maintenance backlog or docking station failure in Bed-Stuy?

themes_detail.label: Dirty condition and litter crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints peaked at 117 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 35.9 per week (226% increase, z-score: 6.87), and litter basket requests spiked 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 1.1 baseline (433% increase, z-score: 5.26), indicating either a sanitation service gap or a localized waste management failure that may still be ongoing.
evidence: Dirty condition complaints: 117 two weeks ago vs. 35.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (226% increase, z-score: 6.87)
Litter basket requests: 6 two weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase, z-score: 5.26)
Community board has standing request to 'increase health and safety inspections' — suggests chronic sanitation oversight
reporting_angles: Sanitation Department explanation: did a street sweeping route get cancelled, delayed, or reassigned two weeks ago?
Community Board follow-up: are litter basket requests being ignored, and what is the backlog for new/repaired baskets?

themes_detail.label: Animal waste on private property
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.4 per week (700% increase, z-score: 5.42), suggesting either an infestation, a rat population surge, or inadequate enforcement of property owner responsibilities that could escalate to a public health concern.
evidence: Unsanitary animal private property complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42, 700% increase)
Dirty condition spike coincides with same timeframe (two weeks ago), suggesting related sanitation degradation
No public health department guidance or rodent inspection data provided; verifiability limited
reporting_angles: NYC Health Department query: were rat complaints or pest sightings filed for the same addresses as unsanitary animal complaints?
Neighborhood canvass: identify specific blocks with complaints and document conditions; interview residents on rodent/pest activity
